summary: The checked-out implementation no longer reproduces the reported compiler assertion for vector bitwise-not or unary negation. Added an end-to-end gfx950 regression for signed and unsigned 32-bit vectors with boundary values, plus an explicit diagnostic for unsupported Python logical-not on Vector values.

tests.what_was_measured: Focused compiler-level unary operator and logical-not diagnostic coverage; 9 tests passed.

Four real-GPU comparisons against NumPy for Int32/Uint32 bitwise-not and modular unary negation, including minimum, maximum, zero, one, and all-bits-set boundary patterns; compiler IR and final ISA were dumped.
Combined regression run; 400 tests passed, including four GPU executions.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed all four kernels. Origin MLIR contains arith.xori/arith.subi on vector<48xi32>; final ISA contains v_not_b32_e32 and v_sub_u32_e32. Raw log: /job/artifacts/j-b82ca60f4cba/gpu-vector-unary-run2.log; dumps: /job/artifacts/j-b82ca60f4cba/dumps-run2.
remaining_limitations: Python logical `not` is intentionally unsupported for Vector because Python defines scalar truth testing rather than elementwise logical inversion; it now raises a direct TypeError. Elementwise predicates should be formed explicitly and consumed as vectors.

Torch/FlyDSL tensor arguments do not expose torch.uint32. The Uint32 vector kernels therefore pass identical uint32 bit patterns through signless i32 memrefs and assign Uint32 at the FlyDSL copy atom; NumPy uint32 is the independent reference.
The issue snapshot's list-valued make_tile spelling predates the current API; the regression uses the current positional make_tile form.

No native C++ files changed. The active source path was /job/repo/python/flydsl and the prepared native bindings path was /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flydsl/_mlir; consequently the native rebuild command was not applicable.
